data.title: OpenAI funding target cut by $10 billion as AI slumps
data.description:
OpenAI has cut its fundraising target by $10 billion as an AI stock selloff and rival Anthropic PBC’s impending public listing complicate its efforts to secure investor commitments, the Financial Times reported.

The ChatGPT maker is now seeking about $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, down from $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation last month, the FT said, citing people with knowledge of the matter.

Some investors have reduced their commitments to OpenAI’s funding round, according to the report. The scaled-back ambitions reflect growing investor unease over the enormous sums being poured into artificial intelligence. The Nasdaq 100 fell 3.5 per cent on Friday.

Bloomberg News reported last week that OpenAI was seeking to raise capital at a $1.25 trillion valuation during the final stages of negotiations.

A group of investors from the United Arab Emirates, including state-backed MGX, is expected to be the largest participant in the round, the FT said. SoftBank Group Corp. and venture capital firms including Sequoia Capital, Coatue Management, Founders Fund and Andreessen Horowitz also plan to participate, according to the report.

OpenAI, Sequoia, Founders Fund and SoftBank declined to comment, the report said. MGX, Coatue and Andreessen Horowitz did not immediately respond to a request for comment, according to the Financial Times.

The fundraising effort faces additional competition from Anthropic, which is preparing to go public next month at a valuation of at least $1.5 trillion, the newspaper said. OpenAI, which raised $122 billion in March, is seeking fresh capital to finance its vast computing ambitions as it prepares for a potential IPO of its own next year, according to the report.

data.title: Signature Global awards ₹500 crore construction contract to B L Kashyap for Gurugram housing project
data.description:
Realty firm Signature Global has awarded a nearly ₹500 crore contract to B L Kashyap & Sons for construction of its luxury housing project in Gurugram.

In April this year, Signature Global tied up with Italian lifestyle brand Tonino Lamborghini to develop a luxury housing project in Gurugram with an investment of nearly ₹2,900 crore.

Now, the company has awarded a construction contract worth ₹496 crore to B L Kashyap & Sons Ltd for its branded residential project, 'Tonino Lamborghini Residences', at Sector 71 in Gurugram.

The project is expected to be completed in 5-6 years, the company said in a statement.

"As India's first Tonino Lamborghini branded residences, the project demands a standard of execution that matches its design ambition, and B L Kashyap experience and engineering capability make them the right partner for it," Lalit Aggarwal, Co-Founder and Vice Chairman, Signature Global, said.

Spread across 12.40 acres, the project comprises 812 premium flats.

Signature Global, one of the leading real estate developers in the country, sold properties worth ₹8,250 crore in the last fiscal and eyes sales bookings of ₹10,000 crore in 2026-27 financial year.

The company has delivered 19.2 million sq ft of real estate since inception.

data.title: ATSL’s notice on re-instatement of written-down AT-1 Bonds: Yes Bank says fully committed to acting in accordance with SC Judgment
data.description:
Yes Bank said it remains fully committed to acting in accordance with the recent Supreme Court (SC) Judgment, which upheld a January 2023 Bombay High Court judgment re-instating the Additional Tier-I bonds that were written-down by the Bank’s then Administrator in March 2020, and applicable law.

The aforementioned statement comes in the backdrop of Axis Trustee Services Ltd/ ATSL (in its capacity as the trustee for the AT-1 Bonds issued by the Bank) issuing a “letter/ notice” to the Bank on October 28, 2026, calling upon the Bank to re-instate the AT-1 Bonds (aggregating ₹8,415 crore) and take all necessary corporate actions within three days.

ATSL has also stated that unless such steps are taken within the timelines specified in its letter, it will be constrained to initiate contempt proceedings before the SC against the Bank and its directors and officers without further notice on the grounds of wilful disobedience by the Bank of the SC Judgement.

Yes Bank, as per its regulatory filing, has informed the Trustee that it is cognizant of the matters and is examining the SC Judgment and its implications in detail. The Bank will take all such steps and measures as are necessary and permissible under the applicable law, it added.

The Bank does not accept the characterisation in your Letter of its conduct as wilful disobedience and the assertions in your Letter are baseless and without merit. The Bank's examination of these matters and evaluation of the consequences is towards compliance with the SC Judgment. The Bank will take all such steps and measures as are necessary and permissible under applicable law.

The Bank said it does not accept the characterisation in ATSL’s letter of its conduct as wilful disobedience, stating that the assertions in the Trustee’s letter are baseless and without merit.

Yes Bank underscored that its examination of these matters and evaluation of the consequences are towards compliance with the SC judgment. Further, it will take all such steps and measures as are necessary and permissible under applicable law.

Responding to the Yes Bank AT1 Bond Holders’ Association’s concerns relating to unpaid coupons on the bank’s two series (coupon rates: 9 per cent and 9.50 per cent) of AT-1 Bonds, ATSL, in a communication to the Association, said its notice to the Bank seeks re-instatement/activation of the said Bonds in the bank’s books and in its register of debenture holders/beneficial owners or their successors.

Further, the notice also wants the Bank to carry out the requisite corporate actions with NSDL and CDSL for reactivation of the two bond series, for reversal of all entries, write-offs and cancellations effected pursuant to the impugned decision and take all steps with BSE and NSE for restoration of the said bonds on their respective platforms, including resumption of trading therein.

data.title: Maruti Suzuki Dzire crosses 3.5 million units of cumulative production
data.description:
Maruti Suzuki India Limited (MSIL) on Saturday said its sedan, the Dzire, has surpassed the milestone of 3.5 million (35 lakh) cumulative production.

Currently manufactured at the company's Manesar facility, Dzire achieved the milestone in about 18 years and 9 months.

"The cumulative production of 3.5 million Dzire vehicles marks a significant milestone in the model's journey.

"Going forward, with increasing manufacturing scale, we remain committed to delivering world-class quality and delighting customers in India and across global markets," Hisashi Takeuchi, Managing Director & CEO, MSIL, said.

Apart from Dzire, Alto, Swift and WagonR are the other models that have crossed this milestone. The company said that Dzire is the first sedan to earn a 5-star Bharat NCAP rating.

data.title: AU SFB data leak: Salesforce says no vulnerability at its end
data.description:
Salesforce on Saturday said it has not identified any vulnerability at its end with regard to the suspected data leak at its customer AU Small Finance Bank.

"Based on currently available information, we have not identified a vulnerability in the Salesforce platform related to this issue," a statement from the customer relationship management (CRM)-focused Salesforce said.

The statement comes a day after AU Small Finance Bank reported that it has started a probe into potential data leak of its vehicle loans customers, following claims that the lender's cyber defences were breached by a group of hackers.

"AU Small Finance Bank is investigating a potential data leak involving a software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform managed and hosted by Salesforce, which holds limited data relating to our vehicle loan customers. We reaffirm that the bank's own systems remain unaffected and all banking services are operating normally," the lender had said in a statement.

The Salesforce statement issued on Saturday said the company does not comment on specific customer issues as a matter of policy and that its teams are proactively engaged to support customers as needed.

The hacker group claimed to have KYC records, identity documents and other important data pertaining to AU SFB, according to threat intelligence platform Hackmanac.

The ScarlettGroup hacking group claims to have breached the AU SFB cyber defence system and threatened to leak sensitive customer and internal corporate data, Hackmanac said in a social media post on Thursday.

"According to the attackers, the compromised information includes KYC records, personal identification documents, PAN and Aadhaar details, credit reports, bank statements, loan applications, signed agreements, insurance records, CRM data, employee information, login histories, and audit logs," Hackmanac said.

However, the threat intelligence platform said that verification of the claim is still pending.

A slew of cyberattacks have been reported in recent days, with the country's largest lender State Bank of India (SBI), private sector lender ICICI Bank, and others as potentially impacted entities.

On October 25, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had also warned of cyberattacks to weaken the Indian economy, and asked all stakeholders to look into the aspect.

He was addressing a gathering after inaugurating the Reserve Bank of India's ₹169-crore data centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar.

data.title: Best Agrolife Q2 profit rises 48% to ₹57 cr
data.description:
Agrochemical firm Best Agrolife Ltd has reported a 48 per cent increase in consolidated net profit at ₹57.46 crore for the quarter ended September 2026.

Its net profit stood at ₹38.93 crore in the year-ago period.

Total income declined to ₹408.57 crore in the second quarter of this fiscal from ₹514.94 crore a year ago, according to a regulatory filing.

During the first six months of this fiscal, the company's net profit grew to ₹98.11 crore from ₹58.85 crore in the year-ago period.

Total income decreased to ₹806.57 crore during April-September period of this fiscal from ₹900.26 crore a year ago.

The company said its revenue was "impacted by irregular monsoon rainfall, delayed sowing, lower crop protection demand in certain markets and heightened competitive intensity during the Kharif season."

The company maintained cost discipline, with operating expenses excluding finance costs and depreciation declining 12 per cent year-on-year in September quarter and 5 per cent in the first half.

Vimal Kumar, Managing Director of Best Agrolife, said: "Q2, FY'27 was a challenging quarter for the domestic crop protection industry. Irregular monsoon rainfall delayed and uneven sowing, moisture stress and limited irrigation availability across several agricultural regions affected crop establishment and the timing of crop protection applications."

These factors, coupled with cautious farmer spending and high competition, created significant headwinds for the business, he pointed out.

"Despite these challenges, we delivered a strong improvement in profitability, with EBITDA growing 30 per cent in Q2FY27 and 45 per cent in H1FY27," Kumar said.

He attributed the margin expansion to strategic shift over the past two years towards a stronger patented product portfolio, besides focusing on cost discipline and operational efficiency.

On the outlook, Kumar said it will depend on the progress of Rabi sowing, soil moisture conditions, irrigation availability and farmers' investment in crop protection.

Best Agrolife is an R&D-based Indian agrochemical company engaged in the development, manufacturing and marketing of crop protection solutions.

data.title: MeitY launches DEPA handbook to enable secure data sharing for AI training
data.description:
India's artificial intelligence (AI) ambitions could receive a boost through wider access to high-quality datasets, with the Union Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) launching a new framework to enable secure data collaboration while protecting privacy, intellectual property and institutional control.

The ministry on Saturday launched the Handbook on Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA) for AI Training at a high-level roundtable in Bengaluru. The handbook was unveiled by S. Krishnan, Secretary, MeitY, with support from the iSPIRT Foundation. The framework seeks to address challenges that often restrict data sharing, including concerns around privacy, confidentiality, intellectual property and institutional control. It establishes a techno-legal framework for purpose-bound data collaboration, allowing institutions to share data for AI training while retaining control over their information.

The framework combines contractual permissions, controlled computing environments and privacy-enhancing safeguards. It also incorporates data provenance, allowing the origin, permissions and use of data to be tracked throughout the AI training process to ensure accountability and transparency. "India's AI ambitions must be matched by the ability to use data responsibly and securely. The DEPA Training Framework enables trusted data collaboration at scale, unlocking access to large-scale datasets for AI training while safeguarding privacy, commercial confidentiality and institutional control," Krishnan said.

Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India Ajay Kumar Sood highlighted that the framework allows AI models to access data without requiring institutions to transfer the underlying information. "Under DEPA, the model travels to the data, rather than the data travelling to the model," Sood said, adding that the approach could facilitate trusted, multi-party and cross-border data collaboration and accelerate scientific discovery. He described the framework as India's contribution to global science diplomacy and efforts to develop an inclusive and responsible global AI ecosystem.

Sharad Sharma, Co-founder of iSPIRT Foundation, described the launch as a significant milestone for India's data economy, comparing its importance with the announcement of the Unified Payment Interface (UPI) in February 2016. Kris Gopalakrishnan, Co-founder of Infosys and Chairman of Axilor Ventures, said the framework could help researchers access diverse datasets to develop more robust AI models while protecting the rights of data custodians and contributors.

The roundtable brought together representatives from government, industry, technology, academia, research and media to discuss trusted data collaboration and its role in advancing AI innovation and public good.

data.title: Lodha Developers makes NCR market debut with Rs.1,700 crore office project
data.description:
BENGALURU, Oct. 31 -- Mumbai-based Lodha Developers Ltd is entering the National Capital Region (NCR) with a Rs.1,600-1,700 crore commercial office project in Gurugram, marking its latest expansion beyond its traditional markets as developers from Mumbai and Bengaluru increasingly turn to the region.

The company, one of India's largest residential developers by sales, has launched Lodha Pantheon at Golf Course Road in Sector 28, Gurugram. It plans to sell the office spaces rather than retain the property for rental income, a senior executive said.

"Our first project in Gurugram has been launched a few days back. It's a predominantly office project that we are selling, and not holding for annuity income," Sushil Kumar Modi, executive director-finance at Lodha Developers, said in an interview.

Last year, Lodha entered into a partnership with Gurugram-based MRG Group to develop two projects. Following the commercial launch, the company is expected to introduce its second Gurugram project, a residential development, this year.

The NCR entry follows Lodha's expansion into Bengaluru a few years ago, where it has been steadily building its portfolio.

The move comes as Gurugram attracts developers seeking to tap demand for premium homes in a market long dominated by DLF Ltd. Mumbai-based Oberoi Realty Ltd made its NCR debut earlier this year, recording Rs.8,109 crore in sales bookings from the launch of Three Sixty North, a luxury residential project spread across 14.8 acres on Golf Course Extension Road in Sector 58.

In September, Bengaluru-based Puravankara Ltd also entered the NCR market with its first project in Greater Noida. Spread across 13.44 acres, the development has a gross development value of Rs.5,200 crore.

Lodha's expansion comes against the backdrop of continued growth in its core business. Its net profit for the July-September quarter rose 28% year-on-year to Rs.1,013 crore, while revenue increased 18% to Rs.4,468 crore, according to a regulatory filing on Friday evening. Pre-sales in the quarter stood at Rs.5,037 crore.

On the back of its first-half performance, the company expects to exceed its full-year profit guidance.

After launching projects worth Rs.4,000 crore in the April-September period, Lodha has a significantly larger residential launch pipeline of around Rs.20,000 crore for the second half of fiscal year 2027 (FY27).

"We are preparing for these launches, but we also have considerable existing inventory that we continue selling and so, our sales are not only dependent on fresh project launches," Modi added.

Beyond residential development, Lodha is seeking to build another growth engine through rental assets, with a particular focus on data centres. The company plans to begin executing its self-funded data centre annuity strategy over the next six months.

It expects annuity income to rise tenfold, from Rs.300 crore in FY26 to Rs.3,000 crore by FY32, as it seeks to increase the contribution of recurring rental income alongside its core property development business.

data.title: Build More or Build Smarter? The Capex Question Facing India's CFOs
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- India is entering another major investment cycle. Steel plants are expanding, data centres are scaling, aerospace manufacturing is deepening. But the biggest capital-allocation question facing CFOs may not be how much to build, it may be whether building more is actually the best way to create the next unit of value.

The distinction matters. India's 1,775 centrally monitored infrastructure projects were sitting on a cumulative cost overrun of Rs.3.41 trillion as of July 2026. A 2020 BCG study found that only around 30% of transformation programmes fully met their targets.

These are not stories of failed execution. They are stories of capital that was deployed, projects that were delivered, and value that still fell short. Which raises the harder question: where is the bottleneck today, and what should the next rupee solve?

That question shaped a roundtable convened by LiveMint and Autodesk in Mumbai, where ten senior finance leaders from steel, aerospace, data centres, engineering, lending and consulting sat across the table from each other. What emerged was not a case for building more or building less, but for building with greater precision.

Consider a greenfield steel plant. Three to five billion dollars. Several years before the first revenue. As Rohit Sharma, Head of Finance at ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India, put it: "Capacity expansion is not the challenge. The challenge is the ROI. You cannot go wrong in any calculations. I cannot say after three years, oh, I made a mistake in the ROI. Your entire IRR will go for a toss." He also emphasized that capital is limited. "We don't have an endless supply, so choosing the right capacity and projects is critical," Mr Sharma added.

That is a useful test for any large capex decision. But it also reveals a quieter challenge. Companies tend to invest where the constraint is most visible - a full order book, a slow production line, an overloaded team. The assumption is that the physical asset is the bottleneck. Often, it is not.

Janesh Moorjani, EVP and CFO of Autodesk, offered a perspective shaped by watching this pattern across the company's own technology investments. Autodesk invested in AI tools that made individual developers measurably more productive - more features, faster code, no loss in quality. Yet the organisation was not shipping products any faster. "The bottleneck shifted from development to experience design and product management," Mr Moorjani said. "And so now we're rethinking how work actually happens in the organisation." The lesson extends well beyond software: investing in one part of the chain without understanding where the constraint moves next can leave the productivity gain stranded.

In aerospace, one Indian manufacturer spent over a decade building engineering capability before the business turned profitable - a sequence that looks irrational on a quarterly earnings call but made strategic sense. As Selvaraj Mudaliar, CFO of Godrej Aerospace, framed it: "Unless engineering capability is built in, buying machinery is just going to increase the depreciation; it will not result in productivity gain."

A machine shows up on the balance sheet. Capability does not. Yet capability may be what determines whether that machine creates value or simply adds to the depreciation line.

The same logic applies at a different scale. In steel, successive expansions from 1.6 million tonnes to 10 million tonnes revealed that scale itself reshapes plant economics. "That's why JSW Steel has one of the lowest production costs," said Nitesh Sanghi, VP of Banking and Finance at JSW Steel. The point is not that bigger is always better. The right sequence of investments matters as much as any single one.

If the constraint is not always physical, it is often informational. A Deloitte survey of 600 senior manufacturing executives found that 74% of manufacturers still run on disconnected legacy systems. For finance, that creates a timing problem. A design change can quietly become a procurement delay, then a production issue, then a cost overrun. By the time it shows up in a financial report, the damage is already done.

That is where the CFO's role is changing fastest. Not from gatekeeper to cheerleader, but from historian to early-warning system.

In data-centre construction, some finance teams are already using AI to close that gap. Rajeev Roy, VP of Finance at Sterling and Wilson Data Center, described how his team uses it: "Without getting into the technical details, I need just two inputs - one from the site team and one from the Planning & Control team. I feed these into AI and simply ask it to 'identify scheduling misses.' It immediately highlights the deviations, prepares a detailed summary, and drafts an email for a quick review before sharing it with the Operations Head."

The value is not just speed. It is timing. Catch a scheduling problem early, and there is still time to fix it. Catch it after the cost has moved, and finance is left explaining what went wrong.

That makes connected data more than a technology issue. It becomes a financial control.

This is also where Autodesk's platform strategy fits into the CFO's changing role. Its tools connect design, engineering, construction, and operations in a shared data environment. When a design change can flow through to the cost model, procurement plan and project schedule, finance gets visibility before the impact reaches the bottom line. The decision is still reversible. The capital is still movable.

Sridhar Kadangode, CFO of Voltas, made the broader point: "In businesses where seasonal demand can concentrate the bulk of the sales in a few months, predictive edge becomes a prerequisite. Finance has to be an enabler; we have to be part of the risk-taking."

Capital Allocation Requires the Right Timing

Better visibility matters. But so does discipline in how capital is phased.

One technology EPC company had planned an investment of around Rs.600 crore to build hydrogen electrolyser manufacturing capacity in India. As the market developed more slowly than expected, the commitment was scaled to Rs.60-70 crore, with the remainder phased to follow actual demand.

Kiran Rahate, Head of Shared Services, Finance at John Cockerill Global Business Services and former CFO of John Cockerill India, marked, "You have to allocate the capital in the right amount and at the right time. As a CFO, that is what the challenge is about."

That restraint is not caution. It is precision - the same discipline the piece began with, applied to timing rather than scale.

The enthusiasm is real. But when every function independently adopts its own tools, the result is often another layer of fragmentation. As Amruta Gaba, Finance Delivery Leader at TCS, put it: "Your job is not to make everyone happy. Focus on bringing everything together." She observed that companies are now stepping back: "Before getting into further initiatives, they want to first understand where everything stands."

And even when the technology is sound, the business case can be difficult to pin down. Pankaj Gupta, CFO of Shapoorji Pallonji Finance, said, "As CFOs in an NBFC, we need clear payback estimates before committing capital. Better knowledge management can connect bid teams with past project experience, helping us make more informed investment decisions."

Gupta raised a related concern: "The person who takes the bid does not speak to the person who has done the project before." When institutional memory is lost, organisations pay to relearn the same lessons. Knowledge management becomes a capital-allocation tool.

Yet none of this argues for permanent caution. In pipe manufacturing, sustained technology investment over the years has brought rejection rates down to roughly one in a thousand. "That type of technology we have developed over the last ten years. The investment in quality has been very good," said Ketan Patel, SVP at Welspun Corp. When the problem is clear, and the investment is targeted, the return follows.

The real risk for India's CFOs is not spending too much. It is spending in the wrong order. A company can add capacity before it has the engineering capability to use it, automate a process before fixing the underlying workflow, or deploy technology without the organisational systems to act on what it reveals.

The defining challenge of the next investment cycle is not whether to spend, but where the next rupee changes the trajectory of the business most meaningfully.

data.title: Binance $6.3B record hack sparks pre-election political chatter
data.description:
Soon after the $6.3 billion hack of Binance, the biggest in crypto history, a few political and administration figures began offering opinions, with a US election approaching on Nov. 3 and voting already having begun in many locations.

President Donald Trump was asked at a news conference on Friday about the hack of Binance. “We don’t know. We’re looking at that, the hack with Binance. They’re saying they’re going to get it back, they’re saying they’re guaranteeing it,” he replied.

The crypto exchange said in a post on X late Friday that it would cover any losses. “We want to be clear about our commitment: Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users.” It added that about $3 billion of the stolen funds had already been frozen in various locations.

It was not clear whether there was any immediate political advantage to be gained from the hack, which was widely attributed to a North Korean group, but Republican and Democratic sides began staking out positions almost immediately.

Wyoming Senator Cynthia Lummis, a Republican and longtime crypto advocate, cited the stalled Clarity Act in a Friday post on X. “Yesterday, hackers stole more than $6 billion from Binance in less than 4 hours, the biggest heist in history. The Clarity Act would have given crypto firms legal cover to freeze suspicious transactions the instant law enforcement calls. Every minute lost is money gone for good,” she wrote.

Related: FBI and Secret Service join response to Binance’s $6.3B hack

Clarity Act stalled over ethics provisions

The Senate on Sept. 15 failed to pass a cloture motion on the Clarity Act that would have established the country’s first regulatory framework for digital assets.

The bill had stalled over proposed ethics provisions that would restrict government officials and their families from issuing or profiting from digital assets while in office.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission then submitted a regulatory action on Sept. 18 covering crypto asset transactions and markets for White House review, as the agency moved forward with its approach to overseeing the digital asset sector.

CFTC Chair Michael Selig referred to crypto market regulation on Friday after the Binance hack, saying in a TV appearance: “This proves our exact point in proposing regulations for crypto markets. … The real issue here is that these are unregulated offshore exchanges and they don’t have the same sorts of safeguards that we have in our financial markets here in the United States.”

Still, Democratic Representative Maxine Waters said in a Friday news release that “The reported $6.3 billion hack of Binance should be a wake-up call to anyone who thinks the cryptocurrency industry can operate without strong accountability. Yet, Trump and Congressional Republicans have been set on pushing a deregulatory agenda that weakens compliance mandates and oversight of the crypto industry, not to mention the Trump family’s own questionable ties to the company.”

Related: Recap: How Binance’s record $6.3B hack unfolded

Trump family and Binance

She also commented on past relations between Binance and the Trump family, saying, “Remember that after Binance’s owner, Changpeng Zhao (CZ), gave over $2 billion to the Trump family’s World Liberty Financial, Trump’s Securities and Exchange Commission’s Chair Paul Atkins dropped the SEC’s slam-dunk fraud case against Binance and CZ, and Trump fully pardoned CZ, allowing him to again get involved with crypto.”

Meanwhile, Binance said it was working with law enforcement, blockchain intelligence firms, token issuers and other exchanges to trace and recover the stolen funds.

The company also promised to publish a postmortem incident report after conducting a full security review.

“We will provide a detailed technical report outlining what happened, the lessons learned and the additional safeguards being implemented,” Binance said.

data.title: What 150 Years of Bubbles Teach Us About the AI Boom — Barrons.com
data.description:
Observers failed to see the impending downturns in 1873, 1929, and 2000. And money is pouring into AI at a much higher rate than it did in those market crashes.

By Kenneth G. Pringle

There have been lots of Irving Fishers through the years.

Fisher was the renowned economist who, on Oct. 15, 1929, said stocks had reached "what looks like a permanently high plateau." Nine days later the market crashed, dropping almost 90% in three years, and it took 25 years to regain Fisher's "plateau."

Fisher isn't alone. The inability to see the proverbial train headed for the station has featured in every crash since the Panic of 1873, which was actually caused by the bursting of an investment bubble in railroads. The dot-com bust of 2000, the subprime-mortgage crisis of 2007-09 — there are more.

Today, with stocks hovering near record highs on soaring investment in artificial intelligence — some say it's already a bubble — it's worth looking back on these disasters, and their run-ups, to see what contemporary observers missed. Maybe it will help us see the next train coming.

"Cooke's Crash," was the New York Herald's headline on Sept. 19, 1873. "A Financial Hurricane in Wall Street."

Jay Cooke was the nation's leading banker, "having accomplished the labors of Atlas," as his hometown Philadelphia Inquirer put it Jan. 18, 1872, selling government bonds to finance Civil War efforts. Success was expected to follow as he applied his nationwide sales network — precursor to the modern investment bank — to the national railroad boom.

But he overshot, laying out $1.5 million ($42 million in 2026) for construction of a second transcontinental line, the Northern Pacific Railway, long before returns would be seen.

Jay Cooke & Co.'s bankruptcy was just the start.

"A Flood of Failures," the Pittsburgh Gazette wrote Sept. 20, 1873. "Runs on Numerous Banks; Business at a Standstill."

The cause was overexpansion, with national trackage doubling in a matter of years. Railroad investment from 1870 to 1890 accounted for 2.24% of U.S. gross domestic product, according to a Brookings study. That is higher than any single investment, from canals (0.66%) to highways (1.13%), to telecoms (1.10%) — at least until artificial intelligence. More on that below.

The boom brought thousands of newcomers to the market, and many got burned.

"I have nothing left, John. It was all in there," the New York Herald reported one man telling another in front of Cooke's Manhattan office.

The bursting of the railroad bubble was followed by a six-year downturn in the 1870s, which was called the Great Depression at the time.

By the 1920s, a newly prosperous America was enjoying the fruits of its industrial revolution. Homes were electrified, telephones installed, and factories churned out waves of consumer marvels.

As the economy roared, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose sixfold, to 381.17 on Sept. 3, 1929, from 63.90 on Aug. 24, 1921.

"The shelves are not piled up absorbing bank money, and the people are buying from hand to mouth, some days motors, other days long hosiery, other days radios, and other days refrigeration machines," Clarence Barron, this magazine's founder, who lived through the 1870s depression, said on June 27, 1927. "[P]eople have the money to follow the fashions and buy what they please."

Barron joined Fisher and others in dismissing concerns of a bubble.

In fact, today's Fed estimates that as much as a fifth of the market had been bought on margin. Investors could put just 10% down, while brokers fronted the rest with money borrowed from the banks. The securities served as collateral. You can see where this is going.

When the market dropped, many neophyte investors weren't prepared for the margin calls demanding more cash. Also squeezed were hardcore speculators, whose money might be tied up with numerous brokers.

As the crash rolled through Wall Street — Black Thursday to Black Tuesday, Oct. 24-29 — thousands went bust. When the banks made their margin calls, brokers sold shares into the reeling market, worsening the rout. The system collapsed.

The Great Depression that followed all but erased memories of the one in the 1870s. It also prompted generations of economists, from Milton Friedman to Alan Greenspan to Ben Bernanke, to focus on avoiding another depression.

It's worked, so far, albeit while ushering in an expansionary new era of national debt. Avoiding investment bubbles has proven more difficult.

The 1990s dot-com bubble foreshadowed today's AI boom, as great pools of capital chased a promising but unproven new technology — the internet — driving company valuations to worryingly high levels.

James K. Glassman and Kevin Hassett played Irving Fisher's role. In September 1999, months after the Dow surpassed 10,000 for the first time, they published Dow 36,000, arguing stocks were undervalued.

"Tomorrow, stock prices could immediately double, triple, or even quadruple and still not be too expensive," they wrote.

Within months, the bubble burst. By November 2000, the 280 firms on the Bloomberg US Internet Index had fallen a combined 75% from their respective highs. One-time darlings like Pets.com, WorldCom, and Global Crossing failed.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq plummeted 78% over the next two years. The Dow staggered sideways before cratering to 6547.05 on March 9, 2009, after the subprime-mortgage crisis. It wasn't until Nov. 2, 2021, that it finally reached 36,000.

Today, money is pouring into AI at an unprecedented rate. Brookings estimates that, by 2032, investment in the AI buildout will amount to 3.63% of GDP. That is half again as much as the railroad expansion of the 1870s, and three times the dot-com boom.

AI has the potential to produce a surge in economic productivity, say supporters, including President Donald Trump, who called it "the oil of the next 20 to 25 years — it's bigger than the internet." Detractors say it's a threat to jobs and maybe even humanity itself.

Yet even if AI does become as big as the internet, it may still leave many losers behind, like Pets.com investors, or the man who had everything in Jay Cooke & Co. That is how crashes go.

Write to editors@barrons.com

data.title: US campaign for control of Congress enters final weekend
data.description:
Key points:
  • Trump administration steps up legal efforts in Alaska Senate race
  • Election officials alarmed by administration's legal actions
  • Record number of early votes cast in person or by mail

By Andrew Goudsward, David Morgan and Nathan Frandino

As the campaign for control of the US Congress reached its final weekend, the Trump administration stepped up its legal intervention in the Alaska Senate race while the number of Americans casting early ballots neared 50 million, a record for a midterm election.

The Department of Justice accelerated its criminal investigation in Alaska on Friday, following reports that aides to a Democratic Senate candidate recruited a retired schoolteacher from a remote fishing village to get on the ballot because he has the same name as the Republican incumbent.

The DOJ, acting on a civil lawsuit that President Donald Trump said he instigated, also filed further motions in an attempt to block the state of Alaska from certifying the Senate results if the Republican incumbent, Dan S. Sullivan, loses a close race on a ballot that includes the nonpartisan candidate Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.

The closely contested race in Alaska is seen as crucial for the Democrats if they hope to take control of the Senate from Trump's Republicans in Tuesday's vote.

PROSECUTOR ALLEGES 'SHAM CANDIDATE' IN KEY ALASKA RACE

It is one of 35 races in the 100-member Senate that will set the tone for Trump's final two years in office. Also up for grabs are all 435 seats in the US House of Representatives.

Early voter participation this cycle has set a record. More than 49 million Americans have already cast ballots, either in person or by mail, according to the University of Florida's Election Lab, up from nearly 46 million who voted before Election Day in the last midterms, in 2022.

A Democratic victory in one or both chambers could result in congressional investigations of the Trump administration, which for two years has enjoyed largely compliant Republican majorities.

Trump has been on a campaign blitz in multiple states over the past month but is not scheduled to travel on Saturday, when there will be a mash-up of American traditions: politics, Halloween and college football across the country. Trump returns to the campaign trail on Sunday in Kansas and Iowa.

The DOJ's top prosecutor in Alaska, US Attorney Michael Heyman, said at a Friday press conference that a recent New York Times article about the supposed recruitment effort had driven a "surge" of FBI resources, adding that he had assigned several prosecutors to the case and that investigative steps were taking place "intensely and swiftly."

The Times reported on Wednesday that aides to Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola recruited Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. to run. Heyman labeled him a "sham candidate" but declined to say what crime may have been committed.

The department had already filed its civil action but, Heyman said, "when the New York Times article hit, that's additional information that accelerated what we've been doing."

Peltola has denied knowing about any effort to recruit the second Sullivan. The retired teacher has denied coordinating with Peltola's campaign.

ADMINISTRATION GETS INVOLVED IN RACES NATIONWIDE

The Trump administration has also sued California to try to prevent the counting of ballots cast by more than 20,000 registered voters who the administration alleged could be noncitizens. It has also sued roughly 30 states and the District of Columbia, seeking unredacted voter rolls, part of a pattern that has alarmed election officials.

A federal judge on Friday ordered the DOJ to stop threatening to prosecute California election officials who do not comply with the Trump administration's directives regarding alleged voting by noncitizens.

Sean Morales-Doyle, director of the voting rights and elections program at the Brennan Center for Justice, said the administration’s actions parallel the tactics undertaken by election deniers in the 2020 presidential election. While the administration is unlikely to win in court, he said, the efforts could create a political atmosphere that leads to official misconduct.

“It's about creating uncertainty, sowing fear, distrust, chaos, hoping that you create the political circumstances in which maybe the lieutenant governor of Alaska does feel pressure to do something that they're not supposed to do. Maybe the governor does start to question things, too,” Morales-Doyle said.

Even so, a bipartisan majority of US voters trust the overall electoral process, with 76% saying they are confident their ballots will be counted accurately, according to a September 30 to October 5 Reuters/Ipsos poll. Some 15% were not confident and the rest were not sure or did not answer the question. Confidence was about equally high among Republicans and Democrats.

data.title: Power bills and data centers cast rare spotlight on utilities in US midterms
data.description:
Key points:
  • US electric bills up 10% since 2024, far outpacing inflation
  • Some states hosting data centers have seen rates spike much more
  • Candidates from both parties vow to control electricity rates

By Laila Kearney

US electricity prices had flown under the radar in past national elections, but they have become a major political issue in this year's midterms as Americans grow angry over rising utility bills and deals for power-hungry data centers.

Nationwide, according to Energy Information Administration data, electricity prices for homes have risen more than 10% since 2024 when President Donald Trump was elected along with Republican majorities in both houses of the US Congress. Higher electricity prices have outpaced the rise in costs for other goods and services.

Power bills have grown even faster in political battleground states of Ohio, Michigan and Pennsylvania, which are also hot spots for new data centers. In some cases, electricity bills have soared by triple the inflation rate.

Many politicians vying for top statehouse seats across the country this year have backed cracking down on utilities. Some have proposed freezing utility rate increases and slashing guaranteed returns, steps that could have sweeping consequences for the country's utility industry.

"It could be the first election to feature utilities and electricity, specifically, as a prominent issue in the midterms," said Charles Hua, executive director of PowerLines, a nonprofit that advocates reforming utility policy to favor consumers. "Part of that is because people's utility bills have gone up and up, and they don't see any end in sight."

Utilities are heavily regulated. State regulators generally must approve utilities’ requests to spend on the grid and to recover those costs through rate increases. Regulators also set the return on equity utilities can earn on their grid investments.

This year, utilities are on track to match last year's record high $31 billion in rate increase requests to regulators, a PowerLines survey showed. Last year's spending was double the previous record.

The investor-owned companies are also expected to carry out a record of nearly $1.3 trillion in capital spending over the next five years, according to an analysis by S&P Global’s Regulatory Research Associates.

UTILITIES SPOTLIGHTED

Seats on nine state public utility commissions are up for election this year, nearly all the US states where voters elect their utility regulators. These include burgeoning data center hubs Arizona and Georgia.

Governors will be chosen in 36 US states this year, and governors appoint utility regulators in states where commissioners are not directly elected.

In Ohio, Democrat Amy Acton has promised to lower energy bills if she is elected governor. Her campaign said she will also appoint a public utilities commission that was "not beholden to utility companies" and work with the state attorney general to crack down on "excessive rate hikes and predatory practices."

Ohio's residential electricity bills have grown by more than 20% over the last two years, according to EIA data.

Acton has also said she supports a data center moratorium. Her Republican opponent Vivek Ramaswamy said he would assure Ohioans living near data centers would not pay electricity bills at all.

BULLY PULPIT

Some governors who are up for reelection have used their political weight to pressure the power industry to keep prices down.

In April, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro announced that prominent utility, PECO Energy Company, had acceded to his demand that it withdraw its proposal with state regulators to increase rates. Shapiro, a Democrat running for reelection, said the move would reduce future utility bills by as much as $34 a month.

He followed up with a letter to more utility CEOs seeking changes in how utilities justify spending and returns on equity.

"The governors are using this crisis on energy affordability as an opportunity to take a deeper dive into the utility regulatory model and see if it makes any sense," said Jamie Van Nostrand, senior fellow at the Kleinman Center for Energy Policy at the University of Pennsylvania and former chair of the Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities.

Power bills tracked low inflation for roughly a decade, and were not an issue in most mainstream elections until last year, when Mikie Sherrill successfully ran for New Jersey governor on the promise of freezing utility bills. She did so the same day she took office.

In Virginia, home to the largest concentration of data centers in the world, Governor Abigail Spanberger took a similar approach, which industry analysts said could offer a playbook for those who win this year’s elections.

Utility advocates say reducing guaranteed returns and freezing rates will not make a meaningful difference in household bills but could lead to a long-term reduction of investments in the grid.

"The grid is America's greatest machine, and it doesn't operate on the political calendar,” said Drew Maloney, president of Edison Electric Institute, a trade organization for investor-owned electric utilities. “It requires consistent investment every year to deliver reliable energy to our customers."

Credit rating agency Fitch downgraded the North American utility sector to "deteriorating" from "neutral" in June, citing political pressure in the midterms to limit electricity bills and utility profits.

For an industry that plans in decades, it is hard to predict the result of short-term political moves aimed at saving money for households.

"I do think the real meat will come after the election," Hua said.

data.title: ICE raids in a California toss-up district spark accusations of voter intimidation
data.description:
Key points:
  • White House directed planned California surge, US official says
  • Union says it knows of hundreds of California farmworkers detained in recent weeks
  • Polls in CA-22 show the Democrat narrowly ahead of the Republican incumbent

By Kristina Cooke and Marisa Taylor

Federal immigration agents have fanned out across California’s Central Valley in recent weeks, stirring fear in Latino communities and allegations of voter intimidation in a toss-up race that could help decide control of the US House of Representatives.

The planned surge in California was announced to agents in early October, an internal email seen by Reuters shows. And it was directed by the White House, according to a US official, speaking on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media.

Unlike past operations in big cities like Minneapolis and Chicago that put hundreds of armed, masked agents on the streets, the surge here has been characterized by small groups of officers moving from town to town in the largely agricultural region. The United Farm Workers union said it knew of hundreds of California farmworkers detained in recent weeks.

In Bakersfield, immigration arrests jumped from one a day for much of the year to nearly 10 per day in mid-October, according to preliminary Department of Homeland Security data. In nearby Wasco, home to just 26,000 people, US Immigration and Customs Enforcement arrested at least seven people in the span of a few days, the data showed.

The arrests have caused widespread alarm in the Latino-majority areas - and could have implications for Tuesday’s midterm elections, in which Republicans will be fighting to retain control of the House and Senate.

In California’s 22nd congressional district, which includes Bakersfield and is 73% Latino, polls have shown progressive Democrat Randy Villegas with a slight edge over six-term Republican incumbent David Valadao.

Villegas told reporters last week that the arrests were a “very clear attempt to try and intimidate our communities before this election."

Valadao said in a statement that he understood "the fear and uncertainty immigration enforcement has created for families throughout our communities," urging the Trump administration to "prioritize the removal of individuals who pose a threat to public safety."

The DHS, ICE’s parent agency, declined to comment on the California operations, citing concerns for officer safety, and did not respond to the allegations of voter intimidation.

“By all metrics, this should be a very close district,” said Thad Kousser, co-director of UC San Diego’s Center for Transparent and Trusted Elections. “Anything that drives voters to or away from the polls could matter.”

President Donald Trump made historic inroads with Hispanic voters in the 2024 election, but polls show public opinion has turned sharply against his immigration sweeps and economic policies.

Just 24% of Hispanic Americans approve of Trump’s performance, the lowest share in either of his presidential terms, a Reuters/Ipsos survey found last month.

In a statement, White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said that Trump’s agenda had made Hispanic Americans “more prosperous and safer” and referred questions on ICE operations in California to DHS.

CLIMATE OF FEAR

Across the Central Valley, ICE has made arrests outside homes and at busy intersections, in strip mall parking lots, gas stations and near schools, according to lawyers, immigration advocates, videos and court records.

"Agents were given the green light to be out and make as many arrests as possible,” the US official said. Officers are also auditing records at local businesses and using employee information to arrest workers at their homes or on their daily commute, the official added.

Maribel Ramirez, a local farmworker, said the arrests have had a chilling effect on political activity in the area. She said that some young Hispanics with US citizenship have told her they are scared to vote, fearing it could expose the addresses of family members without legal status.

Even though voter information is meant to be private, some of “those who can vote won’t do so because their parents are immigrants,” she said.

Ramirez is urging every US citizen she knows to cast a ballot, “but not for anyone in red,” referring to Republicans.

Immigration activists in the area who have been sharing alerts about ICE sightings on social media are also, in some cases, sharing details about the midterm elections.

There are fewer people on the streets in Bakersfield, according to Ana Valencia, who owns a barber shop in town. Some local businesses are offering free delivery to those afraid to leave their homes.

Valencia says she voted early “because I don’t want ICE here, or anywhere really.”

Villegas has made the arrests a campaign issue, criticizing his opponent for voting to triple ICE’s budget and failing “to stand up for immigrant communities.”

Valadao has said ICE is targeting criminals in the community. In an interview with the Sacramento Bee published this week, he said the agency had gone too far in some cases but declined to give examples.

Jason Giannelli, 41, a fourth-generation farmer in Kern County who supports Valadao, said the Republican was “middle of the road” on immigration and “understands that probably ICE is going after the worst of the worst."

FARMWORKERS TARGETED

UFW national Vice President Elizabeth Strater told Reuters that the vast majority of farmworkers detained in recent weeks had no criminal records and some had legal work authorization.

A brother and sister from Mexico were unloading their shopping in a small town in Kern County in late October when immigration agents arrested them, a relative told Reuters, speaking on the condition of anonymity.

It was their day off from work in the fields nearby.

The agents were looking for someone else and did not know whom they had picked up until the handcuffs were on, according to a petition filed by the farmworkers' lawyers in federal court contesting their detention as unlawful.

The sister arrived in the US as an unaccompanied minor more than a decade ago, according to the petition. The brother arrived as a toddler. Neither has criminal records, the petition says.

DHS said it did not have enough information to comment on the case.

On the day of the arrest, the woman's 3-year old daughter was at daycare and her 11-year-old son was on a school camping trip. The children’s father had died suddenly this year, leaving their mother as the sole caregiver.

The 11-year-old returned home excited to see his mother, the relative said. When he heard she had been arrested, he broke down in tears and cried out for her.

The 3-year-old perks up whenever the phone rings, the relative said, asking if her mother is on the line.

data.title: Welspun Living Moves To Net Cash Position, Q2 Profit Jumps 13-Fold
data.description:
The home textiles maker's domestic business grew 28.2 per cent in Q2 FY27, while its cash conversion cycle improved to 44 days from 82 days

Welspun Living has moved into a net-cash position from net debt of Rs 775 crore in March 2026, while its cash conversion cycle nearly halved to 44 days from 82 days, reflecting an improvement in working capital management during the September quarter of FY27.

The home textiles manufacturer reported consolidated net profit of Rs 169.66 crore for Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 14.86 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue from operations grew 16.3 per cent to Rs 2,838.12 crore from Rs 2,440.91 crore.

The company's domestic business recorded 28.2 per cent year-on-year growth during the quarter, while home textiles exports increased 18.3 per cent. Its Welspun brand reported 37 per cent growth, and the flooring business expanded 19.3 per cent.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) increased to Rs 338 crore from Rs 153.3 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Ebitda margin also improved to 11.9 per cent from 6.3 per cent.

On a sequential basis, net profit rose 4.34 per cent from Rs 162.61 crore in Q1 FY27, while revenue from operations increased 1.5 per cent from Rs 2,795.45 crore. Total expenses stood at Rs 2,636.77 crore during the September quarter, compared with Rs 2,609.15 crore in the preceding quarter.

The company also reported an exceptional charge of Rs 7.16 crore during the quarter following the disruption at its Vapi facility in Gujarat due to heavy rainfall and flooding.

Operations at the plant were affected from 23 July. Welspun Living received an on-account insurance payment of Rs 125 crore during the quarter and recognised inventory write-offs, damage to property, plant and equipment, and restoration expenses, net of insurance recoveries, amounting to Rs 7.16 crore.

Commenting on the results, Dipali Goenka, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Welspun Group, said, “Q2 FY27 reflects our continued progress in driving profitable growth and strengthening our financial position.”

She added that the company remained focused on sustaining double-digit growth, maintaining margins in the low teens, improving returns on capital and generating strong cash flows.

“While the external environment remains dynamic and restoration of our Vapi operations remains a near-term priority, we will continue to invest selectively in capabilities, innovation, brands and sustainability to strengthen our competitive position and create long-term value for our stakeholders,” Goenka said.

data.title: Ramkrishna Forgings Q2 Revenue Rises 55% To Rs 1,405 Cr, PAT At Rs 71 Cr
data.description:
Higher revenue and improved operating margins supported the company's quarterly performance, while first-half revenue rose 36.4 per cent year-on-year

Ramkrishna Forgings Limited reported a 54.9 per cent year-on-year rise in consolidated revenue from operations to Rs 1,405.42 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 907.53 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Net profit after tax (PAT) stood at Rs 70.59 crore, against a loss of Rs 9.5 crore in Q2 FY26. The company had reported a PAT of Rs 47 crore in the previous quarter.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) more than doubled to Rs 256.23 crore, up 109.1 per cent from Rs 122.54 crore a year earlier. EBITDA margin improved to 18.2 per cent from 13.5 per cent, an expansion of 473 basis points.

For the first half of FY27, revenue rose 36.4 per cent year-on-year to Rs 2,622.09 crore, while PAT increased to Rs 117.47 crore from Rs 2.29 crore in the year-ago period. EBITDA grew 75.1 per cent to Rs 474.70 crore, with margins improving to 18.1 per cent from 14.1 per cent.

Domestic Demand And Export Activity

Naresh Jalan, Managing Director, Ramkrishna Forgings, said domestic demand remained healthy during the quarter, supported by firm commercial vehicle production schedules. Customer activity across key export markets also remained resilient.

The company, however, is monitoring geopolitical developments in West Asia and changes in global tariff policies, he said.

Forged Wheels Facility Nears Commercial Production

Ramkrishna Forgings said its forged wheels facility near Chennai, established through a joint venture with Titagarh Rail Systems, is nearing commercial production. The facility is expected to help the company enter the forged wheels segment for Indian Railways.

The company is also ramping up its casting operations and adding capacity and value-added products to serve requirements across passenger vehicles, electric vehicles and industrial applications.

It is looking to expand its presence in non-ferrous forgings, including aluminium, titanium, Inconel and Nimonic grades, for applications in aerospace, robotics and semiconductors.

data.title: Tata Motors Launches All-New Punch In South Africa, Prices Start At R224,900
data.description:
The new Punch comes in three variants with two petrol engine options, six airbags as standard and a five-star Bharat NCAP rating

Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (TMPVL) has launched the all-new Tata Punch in South Africa in partnership with automotive group Motus Holdings. The model is priced from R224,900 and will be available in three variants with two petrol powertrain options.

The launch marks another step in the company's expansion of its passenger vehicle portfolio in South Africa. The Punch, which has crossed eight lakh customers in India, enters the market with updated styling, additional technology and enhanced safety features.

The three variants are the Pure+ 1.2-litre 5-speed manual, priced at R224,900; Adventure 1.2-litre 5-speed manual at R244,900; and Accomplished+ S 1.2-litre turbo 6-speed manual at R269,900.

Two Petrol Engine Options

The Pure+ and Adventure variants are powered by a 1.2-litre naturally aspirated petrol engine producing 65 kW and 115 Nm of torque. The top-end Accomplished+ S gets a 1.2-litre turbocharged petrol engine delivering 88 kW and 170 Nm of torque.

South Africa is getting the turbo-petrol option in the Punch range for the first time. The naturally aspirated variants offer City and Eco driving modes, while the turbocharged version gets a dedicated Sport calibration.

The new Punch features wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto as standard across all variants. Depending on the trim, customers get an 8-inch touchscreen or a 10.25-inch HD Harman infotainment system.

Six Airbags Across The Range

Safety equipment includes six airbags as standard across all three variants. The model also carries a five-star Bharat New Car Assessment Programme (Bharat NCAP) rating for adult and child occupant protection.

Other features include electronic stability control, Hill Hold Assist, Hill Descent Control, tyre pressure monitoring and ISOFIX child-seat anchorages.

All three variants come with a five-year or 125,000-km warranty and a two-year or 30,000-km service plan under TataMove, the company's ownership support programme in South Africa.

The launch follows the recent introduction of the Tata Osprey. Tata Motors is working with Motus Holdings and Accordian Investments on its distribution and marketing operations in South Africa.

data.title: Sun Pharma Ordered To Halt Eye Drug Output At Assam Plant
data.description:
Drug regulators flagged quality management failures at the Assam facility, with restrictions covering the manufacture, sale and distribution of ophthalmic products

Drug regulators have ordered Sun Pharmaceutical Industries to halt the manufacture, sale and distribution of ophthalmic products from its Assam facility after identifying lapses in its quality management system. The 20 August order followed a joint inspection by central and state authorities and the company's voluntary recall of around 11 eye-care brands in July.

The action by the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) and the Office of the Drugs Controller, Assam, requires Sun Pharma to demonstrate compliance with quality standards before resuming ophthalmic drug production at the facility. The extent of potential contamination and the impact on patients remain unclear, according to Reuters report.

Regulators Flag Quality Management Lapses

The regulatory action followed a joint inspection of Sun Pharma's Assam manufacturing facility by the CDSCO and the state drug control authority. The inspection identified deficiencies in the systems designed to ensure the quality and safety of pharmaceutical products.

The authorities issued a show-cause notice to the company on 10 August, citing failures in its quality management system. After finding the company's response unsatisfactory, regulators issued the 20 August order restricting the manufacture, sale and distribution of all ophthalmic products from the facility.

The restriction will remain in force until the company submits a satisfactory compliance report and regulators accept its response. Sun Pharma has submitted the report, which is currently under regulatory review, according to media reports.

Recall Covers 332 Batches Of Eye-Care Products

The regulatory action follows Sun Pharma's voluntary recall of around 11 ophthalmic brands in July. The company had informed stockists that the withdrawal was being undertaken as a precautionary measure.

The products included Lotepred 1 per cent 5 ml eye drops, Nepalact OD, Nepalact-Z, Brinzotim 5 ml eye drops and Depopred 2 ml. These formulations are used to treat conditions including eye inflammation, infections and chronic eye diseases.

Regulators have sought additional information on other batches of ophthalmic suspension products. However, it remains unclear whether these batches correspond exclusively to the 11 recalled brands or include products from other brands as well. Based on product packaging, most of the recalled products were manufactured at the Assam facility in Kokjhar village.

Eye Safety Advisory Preceded The Recall

The recall coincided with a patient-safety advisory issued in June by the All India Ophthalmological Society (AIOS), an independent body of eye specialists. The advisory flagged concerns over possible contamination in certain batches of Predmet eye drops.

Regulators have not issued a public health alert following the recall. It also remains unclear whether the recalled products were exported or whether any patients suffered adverse effects linked to the products.

Sun Pharma Says Manufacturing Cessation Was Voluntary

Separately, Sun Pharma Managing Director Kirti Ganorkar addressed the issue during the company's second-quarter FY27 earnings call on 30 October. Ganorkar said the company had voluntarily recalled 11 ophthalmology products and initiated a temporary cessation of manufacturing activities, while keeping the Indian regulator informed. He said the company had undertaken remedial measures to address the concerns, adding that product quality and patient safety remained priorities.

The company indicated that it was working to put the necessary measures in place to resume supplies. The company's compliance report remains under regulatory review. Manufacturing restrictions imposed by the authorities will continue until the regulator is satisfied with the corrective measures.

Ophthalmology Accounts For 3 Per Cent Of Domestic Revenue

The regulatory action comes at a time when Sun Pharma is looking to strengthen its sterile manufacturing capabilities. The company had previously identified the Assam facility as a potential major manufacturing hub for sterile products, a segment it considers an important global growth driver.

Ophthalmology contributes around 3 per cent of Sun Pharma's domestic revenue, according to its FY26 annual report. The therapeutic segment is also among the company's key areas in the US market.

The development adds to regulatory scrutiny of the company's sterile manufacturing operations. Last year, the US Food and Drug Administration halted shipments from Sun Pharma's Halol facility in Gujarat after inspectors identified shortcomings in contamination controls.

data.title: Yes Bank under pressure: Axis Trustee may seek contempt action against bank over AT1 bonds
data.description:
Yes Bank, in an exchange filing, said Axis Trustee Services Limited, acting as the trustee for the private sector lender's Additional Tier 1 (AT1) bonds worth ₹8,415 crore, has asked the bank to reinstate the bonds and undertake all necessary corporate actions within three days.

The trustee has warned that failure to comply could prompt it to initiate contempt proceedings against Yes Bank, its directors and officers before the Supreme Court, alleging wilful disobedience of the court's judgment.

In its October 30 filing, Yes Bank said it had communicated with Axis Trustee Services regarding the Supreme Court's judgment concerning the AT1 bond write-off. The trustee responded on October 28, asking the bank to reinstate the bonds and complete all necessary corporate actions within three days.

Yes Bank said it responded to the trustee on October 30, reiterating its commitment to comply with the Supreme Court's judgment and applicable law. The bank also rejected the allegation of wilful disobedience, describing the assertions in the trustee's letter as baseless and without merit. It added that it was examining the judgement and its implications in detail.

The dispute relates to AT1 bonds worth ₹8,415 crore that Yes Bank wrote off in March 2020 as part of its reconstruction process. The Supreme Court upheld the Bombay High Court's ruling that annulled the write-off, paving the way for the bondholders to seek reinstatement.

The trustee has sought the reversal of the write-off entries with the National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL) and Central Depository Services (India) Limited (CDSL), along with the reinstatement of the bonds on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Earlier, CNBC-TV18, citing sources, reported that Axis Trustee had issued a notice dated October 28, giving Yes Bank three days to restore the bonds in accordance with the Supreme Court's ruling.

data.title: CDSL Q2 results: Profit grows 24% to ₹174 crore; demat account base expands 17% YoY
data.description:
Market Infrastructure Institution Central Depository Services (India) Limited (CDSL) reported a 24% year-on-year increase in net profit to ₹173.9 crore for the second quarter, compared to ₹140.2 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Revenue rose 23.7% to ₹395 crore from ₹319 crore in the year-ago period. Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization (EBITDA) stood at ₹229 crore, while EBITDA margin improved to 58% from 56% a year ago.

Commenting on the results, Nehal Vora, Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer, said, “Despite global macroeconomic volatility, participation in India’s securities market continues to demonstrate resilience. CDSL’s demat account base grew by around 17% year-on-year as of the end of Q2."

He added that this continued growth in market participation drives them to further strengthen their operations and value proposition.

Demat accounts and assets under custody

During the quarter, around 75 lakh new demat accounts were opened with CDSL, as per the company. Its assets under custody (AUC) crossed ₹89 lakh crore.

The company's demat account base grew around 17% year-on-year as of the end of Q2, Managing Director and CEO Nehal Vora said.

Strategic investments and partnerships

During the quarter, CDSL made further investments in India International Bullion Holding IFSC Limited (IIBHL), with the objective of supporting IT infrastructure development, among other areas.

The company also made a strategic investment in the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), an initiative of the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

CDSL said that its subsidiary Centrico Insurance Repository Limited entered into a software development partnership agreement with Shoveltech Solutions Private Limited, which operates in the health-tech domain.

Investor education initiatives

CDSL's Investor Protection Fund (IPF) launched a multilingual investor education film with Amar Chitra Katha, based on its 'The Garden of Prosperity' comic, which is available in 12 languages.

In collaboration with Yuva Unstoppable, CDSL IPF began distributing its investor education comics to nearly 21,000 students across 60 schools. It also launched 'Invest Vidya', an investor education YouTube series.

The investor protection fund conducted over 700 investor awareness programmes across India during the quarter.

data.title: MeitY launches DEPA handbook to enable secure data sharing for AI training
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- India's artificial intelligence (AI) ambitions could receive a boost through wider access to high-quality datasets, with the Union Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) launching a new framework to enable secure data collaboration while protecting privacy, intellectual property and institutional control.

The ministry on Saturday launched the Handbook on Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA) for AI Training at a high-level roundtable in Bengaluru. The handbook was unveiled by S. Krishnan, Secretary, MeitY, with support from the iSPIRT Foundation.

The framework seeks to address challenges that often restrict data sharing, including concerns around privacy, confidentiality, intellectual property and institutional control. It establishes a techno-legal framework for purpose-bound data collaboration, allowing institutions to share data for AI training while retaining control over their information.

The framework combines contractual permissions, controlled computing environments and privacy-enhancing safeguards. It also incorporates data provenance, allowing the origin, permissions and use of data to be tracked throughout the AI training process to ensure accountability and transparency.

"India's AI ambitions must be matched by the ability to use data responsibly and securely. The DEPA Training Framework enables trusted data collaboration at scale, unlocking access to large-scale datasets for AI training while safeguarding privacy, commercial confidentiality and institutional control," Krishnan said.

Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India Ajay Kumar Sood highlighted that the framework allows AI models to access data without requiring institutions to transfer the underlying information.

"Under DEPA, the model travels to the data, rather than the data travelling to the model," Sood said, adding that the approach could facilitate trusted, multi-party and cross-border data collaboration and accelerate scientific discovery.

He described the framework as India's contribution to global science diplomacy and efforts to develop an inclusive and responsible global AI ecosystem.

Sharad Sharma, Co-founder of iSPIRT Foundation, described the launch as a significant milestone for India's data economy, comparing its importance with the announcement of the Unified Payment Interface (UPI) in February 2016.

Kris Gopalakrishnan, Co-founder of Infosys and Chairman of Axilor Ventures, said the framework could help researchers access diverse datasets to develop more robust AI models while protecting the rights of data custodians and contributors.

The roundtable brought together representatives from government, industry, technology, academia, research and media to discuss trusted data collaboration and its role in advancing AI innovation and public good.

data.title: India to meet liquor firms as domestic giants join foreign peers in Scotch dispute
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indian investigators say bulk Scotch doesn’t qualify for the 75% tariff
  • Diageo, Pernod, Allied Blenders, Radico Khaitan among those told, sources say
  • Indian lobby group warns of hit to local manufacturing
  • About 80% of Scotch imports from Britain arrive in bulk

By Aditya Kalra

India's government will hold talks with liquor companies on Monday after domestic firms joined Diageo and Pernod in expressing alarm about a federal investigation into bulk Scotch imports, according to four sources and an industry letter.

In the first major dispute linked to a historic India-UK trade pact implemented in July, New Delhi has told major companies that bulk Scotch imports are not eligible for the tariff reduction to 75% from 150% agreed in the deal.

The International Spirits & Wines Association of India, a group representing Pernod and Diageo , has privately warned New Delhi that the move to exclude bulk Scotch ​imports could undermine the pact.

The Confederation of Indian Alcoholic Beverage Companies (CIABC) has now joined the protest by flagging a hit to domestic manufacturing, according to an October 27 confidential letter to the government that Reuters is reporting for the first time.

Around 80% of Scotch whisky imports from Britain by volume arrive in bulk to be used to make popular brands, and India's $65 billion alcohol industry had hoped the cut in tariffs would bolster business.

Top Indian commerce ministry officials will on Monday hold closed-door talks with several senior executives of foreign and domestic liquor companies to discuss the issue, said the four people who have direct knowledge of the meeting.

The ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside regular business hours on Saturday.

Britain has said it is working with India on the issue, and Scottish government has raised the treatment ‌of bulk Scotch with New Delhi, Reuters has reported. India has not commented on the matter.

Whisky tariffs were a sticking point during years of protracted ​negotiations on a UK-India free trade deal, though India, a whisky-loving nation, ultimately agreed ⁠to halve taxes on certain Scotch imports.

INDIAN PEERS SEEK URGENT INTERVENTION

The CIABC's letter said that if bulk Scotch used in Indian manufacturing was not eligible for the lower tariff, "this could create an unintended incentive in favour of importing finished products."

"Such an outcome would run counter to the objective of strengthening domestic manufacturing under Make in India," it added, seeking urgent intervention to avoid disruptions.

The group’s members include listed Indian majors Radico Khaitan , maker of the 8PM brand, and Allied Blenders and Distillers , maker of Officer’s Choice. CIABC and the companies did not respond to queries. All firms have said they comply with the law.

Allied Blenders said in an investor presentation this week it is “one of the largest bulk Scotch importers” and the UK pact would improve its “luxury portfolio accessibility”.

Import tariff disputes have long been a sore point for foreign investors in ‌India who ⁠have faced demands for large amounts of back tax. Indian officials say they are only enforcing the law of the land.

data.title: Tether's Safety Cushion Nearly Doubles To $8B In A Single Quarter After $1.5B Profit In Third Quarter
data.description:
Key points:
  • Tether's excess reserves nearly doubled to about $7.95 billion at the end of September, from $4.1 billion three months earlier, according to its BDO attestation.
  • The stablecoin issuer earned $1.5 billion in net operating profit in the quarter, and $4.5 billion so far this year, mostly from US Treasury bills and repos.
  • Its $132.4 billion in Treasury exposure is roughly on par with South Korea's holdings, while reserves also included $19.1 billion in gold and $8.4 billion in Bitcoin.

Tether's (USDT) excess reserves nearly doubled in the third quarter, as the issuer of the world's largest stablecoin earned $1.5 billion in profit, mostly from interest on U.S. government debt.

The company's reserves exceeded its liabilities by about $7.95 billion at the end of the September quarter, up from $4.1 billion at the end of June, according to its quarterly attestation, which accounting firm BDO prepared and Tether published on Friday. That buffer was the amount Tether held above what it needed to back every USDT token in circulation.

Tether made $1.5 billion in net operating profit in the third quarter, in line with the previous quarter. It has now earned $4.5 billion so far this year. Most of that came from US Treasury bills and reverse repurchase agreements, which were short-term loans backed by government securities. The profits came even though USDT's supply changed little. Issuance held at about $184 billion through the first three quarters of the year, despite shifts in the crypto market.

USDT’s price continued to trade flat at nearly $1 over the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around USDT remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter around it shifted to ‘high’ from ‘normal’ over the past day.

What Backs USDT?

Tether held $191.5 billion in total reserves at quarter-end, against $183.5 billion in liabilities. Direct and indirect exposure to U.S. Treasury bills made up $132.4 billion. That exposure was roughly in alignment with South Korea's $134.2 billion in U.S. Treasury holdings and above the United Arab Emirates' (UAE) $116.1 billion, according to data from the U.S. Treasury Department.

The reserves also included over $19 billion in precious metals and roughly $8.4 billion in Bitcoin (BTC), valued at Bitcoin's September 30 closing price of $83,621. The rest included $14.2 billion in secured loans, $4.2 billion in public equities and $6 billion in other investments, the attestation showed.

On Reserves

"Our responsibility is to make sure USDT remains dependable when people need it most, including when markets and financial systems come under pressure," CEO Paolo Ardoino said. According to him, earning $1.5 billion in profit while holding "nearly $8.0 billion in excess reserves,” gave them a “strong foundation for that work."

On X, Ardoino said that USDT's user base had reached a record of more than 700 million people across emerging markets. He called the stablecoin "the biggest financial inclusion success story in the history of humanity."
